sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry on intact HEK293 cells confirmed surface display of the FLAG-tagged LY6S-iso1 protein; no functional assay (e.g., receptor binding, signalling) reported for the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: LY6S is a GPI-anchored protein with signal peptide spanning residues 1–26 and the entire mature ectodomain (residues 27–134) extracellular; there is no TM domain and no intracellular region. The only accessible extracellular terminus for tagging is the mature N-terminus, which begins at residue 27 (L). A tag placed upstream of residue 27 would be within the signal peptide and cleaved off, so the junction is unambiguously insert_after_residue=26 (last SP residue G, first mature residue L). The paper in [L1] explicitly reports a FLAG tag at the N-terminus of full-length, membrane-anchored LY6S-iso1 and confirms surface display by flow cytometry on intact cells, satisfying the requirement for a published tolerated insertion on the extracellular face. Position is topology_derived because the paper names 'N-terminus' without specifying a residue number, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists. Full-length GPI-anchored LY6S-iso1 expressed in HEK293 cells via retroviral transduction, with a FLAG epitope tag placed at the N-terminus of the mature protein (after signal peptide). Western blot confirmed the mass shift relative to untagged LY6S-iso1, and flow cytometry on intact cells confirmed cell-surface display.

sources.claim: Furthermore, LY6S-iso1 protein observed in cells infected with retroviral particles coding for the native LY6S-iso1 protein migrated slightly faster than the corresponding LY6S protein that contained a Flag-epitope at its N terminus, conforming to their difference in molecular mass (compare in Fig. 6c , lane 1 [with the Flag epitope] and lane 2 [LY6S protein without the Flag epitope]).Third, by flow cytometry, 5E12 detected cell-surface LY6S-iso1 protein, albeit at low levels, on intact HK293 cells infected with retroviral particles coding for LY6S-iso1

literature_notes: LY6S has a single signal peptide (residues 1–26) and is entirely extracellular from residue 27 to 134 with no TM or intracellular segments (GPI-anchored). The ledger contains one qualifying line (L1): a FLAG-tagged full-length LY6S-iso1 detected on the cell surface by flow cytometry. The paper names 'N-terminus' without a residue number; because the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus (post-SP cleavage at residue 27), the junction is unambiguously after residue 26. No C-terminal tag is supported by the ledger, and a C-terminal tag would in any case be expected to disrupt GPI-anchor attachment signal processing. No internal loop insertions are reported in the ledger for LY6S or close orthologs.
